questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I went there mostly because my boyfriend had to go to Finland for a year. 

But I found it really fascinating to go to a Nordic country where everything was slightly different, but also so surprisingly similar to Denmark. 

The biggest reasons to go are the nature, snowy winter wonderlands, modest people, beautiful downtown Helsinki (e.g. Punavuori), interesting architecture, sauna culture, interesting language and history!

questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: My boyfriend found it, so it was easy for me. However, I heard the housing market is not as crazy as Copenhagen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be careful you don't live too far from campus/good transport. The metro is super convenient of course, so even living in Espoo can be easy. But Helsinki is a slightly bigger city, and much more spread out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: k

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The course registration website was hell, so reserve some time for this. I heard it got better. But also seeing courses in advance was difficult because the search function didn't work well. I found most courses through some lists for potential master's students. So looking at the admissions website might help.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You need to register for an IT-user, you need to find the courses on the SISU system, and then register in a different part of SISU. Then you can use the Canvas system to see the courses and it's contents.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I wrote the exchange student help desk which also gave me a few useful links, but it was a little tough.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty succesful. Just watch out for deadlines too.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start early, but not too early (: Maybe just contact the student exchange help desk as soon as possible and ask them when and where you can do all the registration.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very similar to KU

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very similar to KU, but beware that some courses are tougher than others. And for 30 ECTS, you need 6 courses, since they are all 5 ECTS. You will have 3 at a time. Try to get some easy ones, but I found I could generally guess which ones were easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar to KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus student network was very active, so check that out. The gyms were nice. Oh, and the student cafe's made some reasonable food for very low prices!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus student network was very active, so check that out. The gyms were nice. Oh, and the student cafe's made some reasonable food for very low prices!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Nuoksio National Park, any of the national parks (!!), Lapland, 1-day boat trip to Talinn, try a nice sauna, eat and drink in downtown Helsinki (e.g. Punavuori).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very similar culture. It is a Nordic country after all. People are generally less chit-chatty, and generally more modest. I really enjoyed my time in Helsinki!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Check out the student unions. Ask your welcome buddy about them. They throw all the parties, and I think some are especially welcoming to exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That they were slightly more modest. But expect Finns to be very similar to Danes (:

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it! I loved it so much. See my recommendations on what to do. Make sure to enjoy the nature! And have sauna trip with sauna drinks!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: See my comments on course registration

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know Finland, a little finnish, and learning about our Nordic cousins!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Alcohol was a little pricey.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Loved it! Hyvää Suomi!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
